web.title: RIAE-AKF: Innovation-based Adaptive Estimation
web.description:
- RIAE-AKF is an adaptive filtering algorithm that dynamically estimates both process and measurement noise covariances using innovation and residual data.
- It leverages exponential averaging to update noise parameters, reducing reliance on hand-tuned settings and improving robustness in time-varying environments.
- Practical tuning via a forgetting factor ensures reliable performance, making it well-suited for applications such as dynamic state estimation in power systems.
Innovation-based Adaptive Estimation Adaptive [Kalman Filter](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/kalman-filter) (RIAE-AKF) refers to a class of adaptive filtering algorithms that dynamically estimate the process noise covariance and the measurement noise covariance within an [Extended Kalman Filter](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/extended-kalman-filter-ekf) ([EKF](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/confidence-weighted-extended-kalman-filter-ekf)) framework by leveraging the properties of the innovation and residual sequences. The objective is to achieve robust on-line state estimation in scenarios where the authentic noise characteristics are unknown or time-varying, as is common in complex dynamical systems such as synchronous machines in power networks. The RIAE-AKF systematically adjusts and at each iteration using recurrence relations based on innovation and/or residual statistics, alleviating the need for ad hoc, hand-tuned noise parameters and providing greater resilience to initial mis-specification compared to conventional EKF approaches ([Akhlaghi et al., 2017](/papers/1702.00884)).

web.title: On the Identification of Noise Covariances and Adaptive Kalman Filtering: A New Look at a 50 Year-Old Problem
web.description:
The Kalman filter (KF) [23] is the optimal state estimator for linear dynamic systems driven by Gaussian white noise with measurements corrupted by Gaussian white noise.^1^ In the classical design of a Kalman filter, the noise covariance matrices are assumed known and they, along with the system dynamics, determine the achievable filter’s accuracy. However, in many practical situations, including noisy feature data in machine learning, the statistics of the noise covariances are often unknown or only __partially__ known. Thus, noise identification is an essential part of adaptive filtering. Adaptive filtering has numerous applications in engineering [36], machine learning [9], econometrics [11], weather forecasting [10], [20], [35], [46], to name a few.
We were motivated by the following learning problem: Given a vector time series and a library of models of system dynamics for the data (e.g., a Wiener process, a white noise acceleration model, also called nearly constant velocity model, or a white noise jerk model, also called nearly constant acceleration model), find a suitable process noise and measurement noise model and the best system dynamics for the time series. The problem we consider in this paper is limited to finding a suitable process noise and measurement noise covariance for a given dynamic model.

A novel six-step solution approach via a successive approximation and adaptive gradient descent scheme with a new objective function to obtain the unknown noise covariance matrices __Q__ and __R__, as well as the steady-state Kalman filter gain __W__, and the steady-state state prediction covariance matrix P¯ or the updated state covariance matrix __P__, is proposed. This ensures positive definite __Q__ and positive definite __R__, as well as P¯ and __P__.

web.title: An adaptive Kalman filter for radar tracking application
web.description: Adaptive filtering is trying to determine the statistic parameters of the dynamic system based on the observable data, and then using them to approximate the system state. Adaptive Kalman filtering theory has been paid much attention and various algorithms have been studied and applied in signal processing. A simple approach is to estimate the process noise variance by mean of a scale factor [3], [4]. These algorithms differ from each other by the way in which the scale factor is computed. In this paper a novel algorithm for the scale factor calculation is investigated. Every time the process noise covariance is updated by a time-average of the sum of the diagonal elements of the innovation covariance, which is computed with a weight coefficient, if their difference is larger an predetermined threshold in order to degrade the influence of probabilistic character of the innovation. The algorithm is applied to the Extended Kalman Filter to simulate its performance in two-dimensional tracking, in which the radar measurement is carried out in polar coordinate system and the target is tracked in the Cartesian system. The simulation results demonstrate that the novel adaptive filter is much robust to the sudden changes of target motion compare to the conventional Kalman filter and its performance is almost as good as conventional Kalman filter with suitable statistical properties of dynamic model.

web.title: A Single-pass Noise Covariance Estimation Algorithm in Multiple-model Adaptive Kalman Filtering
web.description: In [5], we proposed an enhanced covariance estimation method based on a sequential mini-batch stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm that required multiple passes through the data as well as a method to detect changes in noise covariances when applied to non-stationary systems. In this paper, we propose a single-pass adaptive Kalman filtering algorithm for non-stationary systems, wherein the process and measurement noise covariances continuously change, and the system behavior can stem from a member of a known subset of models.

web.title: Adaptive Kalman Filtering by Covariance Sampling
web.description:
Kalman filter is the minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimator which is traditionally employed for this purpose. However, the efficacy of this estimator deteriorates if the system noise statistics are not known a priori. Among the noise statistical parameters, the measurement noise covariance recovery is most important as it directly regulates the impact of the measurements on the system estimations. In addition, this parameter is the key factor in many multi-sensor applications including sensor fusion [2] and sensor selection [3], [4] as it defines the informativeness of the sensory data.

In a more systematic approach, the parameters of the system are estimated using adaptive techniques. Various adaptive schemes have been proposed since the advent of the Kalman filter which benefited many modern applications in robotics [8], [9], surveillance and tracking [9], [10], machine learning [11], [12], navigation [13], [14], and others.

This work proposes a covariance distribution sampling approach to take advantage of the noise statistics in the approximation of the system posteriori. Assuming the measurement noise to be white and Gaussian, its covariance priori is sampled and the resultant posteriori distribution is marginalized over all samples, which yeilds a Mixture of Gaussians (MoG) the components of which are computed exploiting Kalman filtering. Since it is known that the system state follows a Gaussian distribution, a Gaussian Mixture Reduction (GMR) technique is employed to reduce the resultant MoG to the closest Gaussian distribution. In addition, the measurement noise covariance of the system is updated by collapsing the propagated estimated samples to enhance the accuracy of the estimations.
